absent: Locking discipline for CPU operations table, feature register descriptors and capability state.
Interrupt, preemption and concurrency rules for capability detection and enable paths.
Contents of supported CPU operations tables and ACPI enable method resolution.
Population, update timing and synchronization of sanitized feature register values.
Semantics of alternative patching, system capability masks and finalization sequencing.
Full compat system call translation and signal handling beyond layouts and predicates.
Hypervisor mode build configuration and KVM context distinctions beyond name checks.
Error recovery beyond logged warnings for missing device nodes and properties.

findings.text: Each examined arm64 header carries a single inclusion guard that prevents repeated processing within one translation unit.
Compat user view uses narrow legacy widths: user and group identifiers each occupy sixteen bits and link counts use signed thirty two bits.

Compat status record conveys file identity and metadata for legacy callers, including device, serial, mode, link multiplicity, ownership, special device, size and block accounting, three timestamps with nanosecond companions, plus reserved words, with device packing differing by endian selection.

Compat filesystem status record reports type, block sizing, total plus free plus available counts, file node totals and free counts, filesystem identity, name length bound, fragment size, flags and spares.
Compat minimum signal stack size is 2048 bytes.

Compat stack accessor derives the legacy stack pointer from current register state. Predicates report compat mode for the current task and for a given thread by testing TIF_32BIT, with an alternate build that always reports false.

Assembly preamble and pointer authentication handling are build dependent. One variant emits an architecture directive and strips instruction authentication with a hint bound to a fixed register, while the other emits nothing and returns pointers unchanged, with separate selectors for kernel and user instruction pointers.
Return address acquisition is wrapped so kernel instruction authentication is removed before the caller address is exposed.
Thirty two bit identity block groups debug, instruction set, memory model and media capability registers as narrow unsigned words.

Sixty four bit identity record begins with a kernel object for exposure, then cache, timer and silicon identifiers, followed by snapshots for debug, instruction set, memory model, performance and vector plus matrix extensions, and embeds the thirty two bit block.
Boot method table names the method and provides staged hooks for init, preparation, boot and post boot work, extended under hotplug with checks and actions for disabling, dying and reaping.
Boot CPU setup targets CPU zero. Per CPU init resolves the configured enable method name and binds the matching operations entry, failing when the name is missing or unsupported.

Enable method resolution uses device tree when ACPI is disabled and ACPI tables otherwise. Missing nodes or properties are diagnosed, with boot CPU quiet to avoid spurious reports, and operation lookup scans a null terminated table by name equality.

Feature namespace holds up to 192 entries. Software override bit positions are 0 for no randomization, 4 for hypervisor mode and 8 for read only data. A helper forms capability identifiers by prefixing.

Field safety policy offers exact value, lower safe, higher safe and higher or zero safe orderings. Companion flags record signedness, user visibility and strictness, with visibility optionally conditioned on build configuration.
Field descriptor records signedness, visibility, strictness, safety ordering, bit offset and span, plus a fallback value for exact matching.
Override state pairs value with mask. Register descriptor carries name, strict and user masks, system and user values, optional override link and field table link.

Scope occupies bits 0, 1 and 2 for local CPU, system and boot CPU, combined by a mask with short aliases. Bits 4 through 7 govern late permission, late optionality, conflict panic and early matching, combined into named composites for errata, system, weak local, early local, boot restricted and strict boot behaviors.

Capability entry holds description, numeric identity, type flags, scope aware matcher, broad enable hook, variant payload for errata ranges or register bounds with hardware tagging, optional alternate detector list and CPU mask.

Scope is extracted by masking type flags and early matching tests a dedicated bit. Multi entry matching succeeds if any listed detector succeeds. Context checks distinguish hypervisor flavors and their union. Iteration walks set bits in the system mask and finalization state gates boot queries.
Sanitized access resolves a descriptor by ordered search and returns its system value, yielding zero when absent. Strict lookup warns on missing entries while the quiet variant returns null silently.

Extraction isolates a bit span with signed or unsigned meaning, defaulting to four bits. Related helpers provide masks, merged user views and numeric values, plus predicates for mixed endian, thirty two bit levels, vector, matrix and partitioning support, reading live registers for local scope and sanitized values otherwise.

Final capability queries before finalization trap. Unknown register requests warn. Zero width extraction warns once and uses a nibble. Missing enable data logs, with boot CPU exempt from some warnings.
CPU control moves through early init, preparation, boot and post boot stages, with optional hotplug path through permission check, disable, die and reap.

Capability handling flows from detection by matchers to system wide enable, where hooks run on all CPUs and must self guard when action needs local presence, with lists allowing several detectors to share one identity while avoiding repeated enable.
Early boot and capability code can bind CPU operations and query sanitized feature state through boot init, per CPU init, sanitized read and descriptor lookup.
